claims.text: A connector integrates Glean with a system where content lives.
claims.excerpt: A Glean connector integrates Glean with a platform, service, or application where your content lives

claims.text: Indexing connectors index content, mirror source permissions, and keep data current in the tenant.
claims.excerpt: They let Glean index content, mirror permissions from the source, and keep that data current in your isolated tenant.

claims.text: Connector function 1: data fetching, including the permissions map.
claims.excerpt: Data fetching: Connectors fetch data from connected applications and store the information in Glean's system.

claims.text: Connector function 2: content and permission parsing.
claims.excerpt: Content parsing: Connectors parse item content (for example, title, body, comments, media) and permissions

claims.text: Connector data is encrypted in transit and written to disk only in the tenant.
claims.excerpt: Data is end-to-end encrypted in transit and only written to disk once it reaches your tenant.

claims.text: Glean needs content, people, and activity data to build the Knowledge Graph.
claims.excerpt: Activity data Creation, modification, editing, viewing, and sharing timestamps and user information

claims.text: Activity signals drive relevance ranking.
claims.excerpt: Connectors collect activity signals - such as views, edits, and shares - that Glean uses to rank search results by relevance

claims.text: Native freshness uses webhooks or incremental crawling.
claims.excerpt: Connectors capture changes as quickly as the source and connector allow, often through webhooks or incremental crawling.

claims.text: Identity resolution aligns identities across systems.
claims.excerpt: Identity resolution: Glean aligns identities across systems

claims.text: Metadata-only results cannot ground Assistant.
claims.excerpt: Can't be used for GenAI Glean Assistant will not be able to summarize the content

claims.text: The Enterprise Graph is layered on the index and identity/permission structures.
claims.excerpt: connectors populate the index and associated identity and permission structures; the graph interpretation layers on structure and signals derived from that data.

claims.text: Native connectors are purpose-built per application and call source APIs directly.
claims.excerpt: Purpose-built for specific applications (for example, Slack, Salesforce, Google Drive). They call source APIs directly

claims.text: Web history connectors surface page titles from a user's browsing history, private to that user.
claims.excerpt: The Glean browser extension makes page titles from users' browsing histories searchable for specific apps. These results are private to the individual user

claims.text: Push API connectors push data through the Indexing API for custom, self-hosted, or firewalled systems.
claims.excerpt: Ideal for custom applications, self-hosted environments, or systems behind firewalls. Data is "pushed" into Glean via the Indexing API

claims.text: Shared push connector code may have limited support.
claims.excerpt: Push API connector code may be shared between customers or Glean partners; support for such code may be limited.

claims.text: Partner connectors use the Indexing API and are built and supported by the partner.
claims.excerpt: Built and maintained by Glean technology partners. These connectors use the Indexing API to push data into Glean, but the integration is developed and supported by the partner organization.

claims.text: Tools (including MCP) act at request time and do not make content searchable.
claims.excerpt: Tools retrieve current data or perform actions at request time. They don't make source content searchable.

claims.text: Custom Metadata works on any datasource without re-indexing.
claims.excerpt: It can attach metadata to documents from any datasource, including native connectors, without re-indexing the source document.

claims.text: Indexed access uses the mirrored permission snapshot.
claims.excerpt: Latency is typically low, and Glean applies the permission snapshot that was mirrored during crawling and incremental updates.

claims.text: The source may enforce access again at click time.
claims.excerpt: Opening a result usually sends the user to the source system, which may enforce access again at click time.

claims.text: Three access modes: indexed, live, hybrid.
claims.excerpt: indexed (crawled ahead of time), live (fetched at query time), or hybrid (a mix of both)

claims.text: The runtime chooses index, live, or hybrid paths per request.
claims.excerpt: Choose data paths: Prefer index, live retrieval, or hybrid, per connector capabilities and query needs.

claims.text: Live access can require per-user authentication.
claims.excerpt: Some connectors require individual end users to authenticate before live access works for them.

claims.text: Indexed mode suits bulk corpora and historical or cross-document questions.
claims.excerpt: Docs, wikis, tickets, knowledge articles, code, and other bulk corpora; historical or cross-document questions.

claims.text: Live retrieval suits freshness-dominant data or data impractical to index.
claims.excerpt: Email, calendar, chat, or other data where minutes-to-hours freshness dominates, or where continuous full indexing is impractical or undesired.

claims.text: Example: NetSuite MCP uses each user's own credentials and role at request time.
claims.excerpt: NetSuite MCP provides real-time access at request time using each user's own NetSuite credentials and role.

claims.text: New deployments set up catalog MCP integrations from Connectors.
claims.excerpt: Glean deployments created on or after September 22, 2026, use Connectors to set up catalog-backed MCP integrations.

claims.text: Custom or unlisted MCP servers use a separate setup path.
claims.excerpt: For a custom or unlisted remote MCP server, use Connect remote MCP servers to Glean instead.

claims.text: One app can have separate indexing and tools entries.
claims.excerpt: A single application can have more than one catalog entry. For example, one entry might index content while another provides MCP tools.

claims.text: Example of a hybrid design: the MCP entry depends on the indexing connector.
claims.excerpt: NetSuite MCP depends on the native NetSuite connector being set up.

claims.text: For live data, consider custom actions or MCP.
claims.excerpt: Consider custom actions or MCP integration for querying live data

claims.text: For large structured data lakes, query with an action or MCP server.
claims.excerpt: For large structured data lakes leverage a custom action or MCP server to query the data

claims.text: Custom connectors ingest data from sources without native support.
claims.excerpt: specialized integrations built to ingest and index data from sources that are not natively supported

claims.text: Offset pagination is unstable under writes.
claims.excerpt: Offset pagination is unstable against a source being written to during the crawl.

claims.text: Fallback when no API: export to storage.
claims.excerpt: Can the Source System Export Content to an external data storage location

claims.text: Use an existing connector before building a new one.
claims.excerpt: Work to leverage an existing connector first before building a new one

claims.text: Glean is not a time-series or sensor analytics platform.
claims.excerpt: Glean is not a data analytics platform for time series or sensor data

claims.text: Scoping asks about native and web-crawler options first.
claims.excerpt: Is there an existing Native Connector for this Source System, or can it be crawled using the native Glean Web Crawler datasource?

claims.text: No activity means weaker ranking.
claims.excerpt: There would be limited signals available due to no activity being pushed, so rankings of search results will be suboptimal.

claims.text: Native and custom connectors use separate namespaces.
claims.excerpt: Native and custom connectors occupy separate namespaces in Glean.

claims.text: Artifacts scoped to a native connector do not carry over.
claims.excerpt: agents, saved searches, app filters, and pinned results scoped to the native connector won't automatically recognize content in the custom connector.

claims.text: Custom results can be outranked without signals.
claims.excerpt: Results from your custom connector are more likely to be outranked by results from other connectors due to stronger ranking signals.

claims.text: Partner maintains published connectors.
claims.excerpt: Glean expects the partner to maintain and support this connector.

claims.text: Permission mirroring depends on correct connector configuration.
claims.excerpt: If a user cannot access an item in the source, they should not see it in Glean-assuming the connector and configuration are correct.

claims.text: Choose hosting before building.
claims.excerpt: Choose where it runs before you build, because it determines how secrets, scheduling, and networking are handled.
